description: We are willing to take this project because astronauts face many health challenges during space missions. We want to use AI technology to monitor their vital signs, detect abnormal health conditions and provide emergency alerts. Through this project, we aim to improve astronaut safety, support early medical attention and contribute to future space exploration using innovative biomedical technology.
summary:
*SUMMARY*
Radiation is one of the biggest threats to astronauts living beyond Earth's protective atmosphere. As Canada prepares for Moon and Mars missions, CSA is investing in technology to understand exposure and protect astronaut health.
Neutron radiation accounts for about 30% of total radiation on ISS, and it is especially harmful because it can cause serious biological damage and requires specialized protection.
To address this, CSA awarded a $5.5 million contract to Bubble Technology Industries to develop CANS, a compact, autonomous instrument to measure neutron radiation in space.
For over 25 years, ISS has been a test bed for technology, and Canada has expertise from MOSFET, EVARM, and Radi-N and Radi-N2 experiments.
CANS works continuously and autonomously, improving on previous methods. Its data will help reduce health risks for astronauts, and support Earth uses like cancer therapy, aircrew protection, nuclear threat detection, and public safety.
